title: Atoms & the Periodic Table
summary: What is inside an atom, and how did scientists find out without ever seeing one? This unit follows the story from Kanad and Dalton to Rutherford and Bohr, builds atoms from protons, neutrons and electrons, explains electron shells and isotopes, and uses them to make sense of the periodic table.

ib.statementOfInquiry: Scientific models of the atom have changed over time as new evidence appeared, and the patterns they reveal let us organise and predict the behaviour of every element.

factual: What particles is an atom made of, and where are they?
What do the atomic number and mass number tell us?
How is the periodic table arranged?
conceptual: Why do scientific models change over time?
How does the arrangement of electrons explain the patterns in the periodic table?
debatable: Is a model 'wrong' if it is later replaced by a better one?
Should the credit for a discovery go to the person with the idea or the person with the evidence?

cbseChapters: Class 9 Exploration (2026) Ch 9: Atomic Foundations of Matter (Dalton, atomic mass)
Class 9 Exploration (2026) Ch 8: Journey Inside the Atom (Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr, shells, valency, isotopes)
